To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ornament was a system of visual and material ordering that was not necessarily subserviant to the work of art, that it was a means of communication, and that ornament is not a category of style.

ornament in the sixteenth-century Netherlands was: • A system of ordering, not an ornament system, • A system that cut across the divide between the vernacu- lar and the classicizing, • A system of relationality, • A system whose rules were not always followed, but were nevertheless respected, • A system with its own history, and • A system that was both a sign of wealth and status and an agent of pleasure and curiosity.

ornament is not an aesthetic category, but an historical one; ornament is not a decorative or superficial addition, but an integral part of an object or building; and, ornament is not a mere stylistic device, but a system of ordering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which early modern ornament was understood, used, and perceived.
the ways in which the ornament of the sixteenth-century Netherlands was a part of a system, and with the systems that it created.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ornament was not merely decorative but was also a means of ordering, of organizing, of structuring, of making sense of a given subject or object.
ornament in the sixteenth-century Netherlands was a system, and that the systems were many, not one, and that each system was governed by its own rules, and that the rules were many and not one.
ornament is the art of embellishment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the relationship between the ornamentation of the object, and the object’s meaning and function.
the ornamentation of a given object was a matter of its function and the status and taste of its owner.
we have been able to show the importance of ornament as an aesthetic category, and the need to understand ornament in terms that go beyond its role as mere surface decoration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ornament was not just a matter of surface decoration but also of structure.
ornament in the sixteenth-century Netherlands was not a decorative add-on, but rather a system of visual organization that was essential for the creation of a coherent and meaningful work of art.
ornament was a powerful, complex, and flexible means of expression in early modern culture, and that it deserves to be considered as a system of ordering in its own right.
